summary: Oklahoma's first fire tower (1926); its 1974 Aermotor replacement was halted by a footings error, leaving the cab on a 75-foot deck instead of the planned 100 feet.

facts.status_note: Described by NHLR as still in active service; page last updated 2016, not independently reverified.

events.note: Original wood tower erected; first fire lookout tower in Oklahoma.
Original tower replaced with a 100-foot wood tower.
The 1937 wood tower was destroyed in a storm. (Only NHLR mentions the cause; the Forestry Service page just notes the 1974 steel tower's construction.)
Replaced with a steel Aermotor tower; construction was meant to reach 100 feet but a measuring error at the footings halted it at 75 feet, where a deck and the 7x7-foot cab were placed.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 16, 1997, as US 238 / OK 1, nominated by Patrick McDowell of Oklahoma Forestry Services.

corrections.evidence: Both NHLR and the Oklahoma Forestry Service lookout page say the 1974 Aermotor tower was meant to reach 100 feet (30.5 m) but construction was halted at the 75-foot (22.9 m) level because of a footings measuring error; the cab and deck sit at that 75-foot level, so the as-built height is closer to 22.9 m than 30.5 m.

sources.title: Carnasaw Mountain — Oklahoma Lookouts, McCurtain County, Oklahoma Forestry Service

notes_for_editor:
Two independent, consistent sources cover the build/rebuild history well (1926 original, 1937 rebuild, 1974 storm loss and Aermotor replacement with the footings-error deck), but neither says anything about staffing history, specific fires spotted, or current public access — those fields stay unknown. Flagged a height correction: the record's 30.5 m (100 ft) reflects the tower's planned height, not the 75 ft (22.9 m) it was actually built to after the footings error; worth a human call on which figure the map should show. Did not refetch nhlr.org or firetower.org per the guide; no additional web search was needed given the two cached sources agreed.

Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): the draft had the tower 'watching over the surrounding Ouachita National Forest' and being in active service 'as of' its 1997 register listing, both attributed to NHLR. Neither is in the NHLR text — the page only says the tower 'is still in active service' as of its last update (Nov 2016), with no statement about what it watches over or forest-boundary claims. Softened both in the story and removed the unsupported forest-duty claim. Also split the 1974 storm-destruction citation to NHLR only, since the Forestry Service page never mentions a storm. Rewrote the Aermotor-rebuild paragraph, which had tracked the NHLR sentence structure too closely (same clause order and several repeated phrases like 'measuring error at the footings').
